summary: Enterprise AI agent platform built around reliable customer-experience workflows.
editor_note: Customer-service agents need correctness more than another fluent chat layer. Scaled Cognition describes schema-checked actions and simulated backend tests. AgentTwin turns past support conversations into draft behaviors for human policy review. That is more inspectable than a blanket promise of no hallucinations. Whether the controls survive conflicting policies and failing enterprise systems remains untested here.

sources.label: Scaled Cognition official Series A announcement

product_evidence.claim: The APT product page says the model validates parameters against system schemas before executing functions and confirms system execution before replying.
AgentTwin describes importing historical voice, chat, or email conversations to draft agent behaviors, followed by human review of policies and constraints before validation.

The platform offers a browser-based builder and Python SDK; GenAPI simulates backend responses and customer scenarios so teams can evaluate correctness and policy adherence before connecting live systems.
Scaled Cognition lists hosted, customer VPC, and on-premises deployment options, with action and policy-check logs for reviewing agent behavior.
Genesys announced a partnership to combine its Cloud platform with Scaled Cognition's action models for virtual agents; the announcement describes planned capabilities, not measured customer results.

market_context.primary_user: Enterprise CX engineering and operations teams defining support policies, connecting transactional APIs, and testing voice or chat agents before customer-facing deployment.
market_context.differentiation: Its documented workflow connects transcript-derived behavior specifications, schema-constrained actions, simulated backend tests, and deployment controls in one CX agent stack.
market_context.why_now: The June 2026 Series A and the published AgentTwin and GenAPI workflows provide milestones for assessing whether its reliability approach can move beyond product demonstrations.

risks.claim: Schema checks and simulations do not by themselves establish reliability under conflicting policies, partial API failures, or long-tail customer requests.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment; no API integration, independent benchmark reproduction, or production customer evaluation was performed.

risks.claim: Implementation effort, commercial pricing, and the scope of any contractual reliability guarantees require a vendor evaluation.
risks.basis: The public product and demo surfaces describe capabilities but do not establish these terms for a particular deployment.
